ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A small generator contains a rectangular coil with $n=100$ turns and an area of $S=0.10\mathrm{m}^{2}$. The resistance of the coil is negligible. Under the action of an external force, the rectangular coil rotates at a constant angular velocity $\omega=100\pi\mathrm{rad/s}$ around a fixed axis $\mathrm{OO^{\prime}}$ perpendicular to the direction of a uniform magnetic field $B=0.10\mathrm{T}$. The two ends of the generator coil are connected to a resistor with $R=100\Omega$, forming a closed circuit.

1. Find the maximum value of the induced electromotive force generated when the coil rotates.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A small generator contains a rectangular coil with $n=100$ turns and an area of $S=0.10\mathrm{m}^{2}$. The resistance of the coil is negligible. Under the action of an external force, the rectangular coil rotates at a constant angular velocity $\omega=100\pi\mathrm{rad/s}$ around a fixed axis $\mathrm{OO^{\prime}}$ perpendicular to the direction of a uniform magnetic field $B=0.10\mathrm{T}$. The two ends of the generator coil are connected to a resistor with $R=100\Omega$, forming a closed circuit. 1. Find the maximum value of the induced electromotive force generated when the coil rotates.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a magnetic pole labeled N, on the right side is a magnetic pole labeled S, and a rectangular coil is placed in the middle. The coil rotates about a fixed axis labeled O and O′, and the two ends of the coil are connected through a wire/brush structure to the external resistor R, forming a closed circuit. Reasoning: It is known that the number of turns of the coil n=100, the area S=0.10 m^2, the magnetic induction intensity B=0.10 T, and the angular velocity ω=100π rad/s. When the coil rotates uniformly in a uniform magnetic field, the magnetic flux of a single turn can be written as Φ=BS cos(ωt). For an n-turn coil, from Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, e=-n dΦ/dt=nBSω sin(ωt). Therefore the maximum value of the induced electromotive force is E_max=nBSω. Substituting numerical values: E_max=100×0.10×0.10×100π=100π V≈314 V. The external resistor R does not affect the maximum value of the electromotive force.
